questions.text: A cylindrical block of mass M and area of cross-section A is floating in a liquid of density \rho with its axis vertical. When depressed slightly and released, the block oscillates vertically. The period of oscillation is :
questions.solution: Restoring force F = -(\rho A g)x. Spring constant k = \rho A g. Time period T = 2\pi\sqrt{M/k} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{M}{\rho A g}}.

questions.text:
Match Column-I (Electromagnetic Wave) with Column-II (Source/Mechanism):

| Column-I | Column-II |
| :--- | :--- |
| A. Radio wave | I. Rapid acceleration of electrons in aerials / vacuum tubes |
| B. Microwave | II. Due to change in vibrational modes of atoms |
| C. Infrared wave | III. Due to inner shell electrons transitioning from higher to lower levels |
| D. X-ray | IV. Due to rapid deceleration of high-energy electrons (Bremsstrahlung) |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: Radio waves are produced by accelerated electrons in antennas (I), Microwaves in special vacuum tubes (klystrons/magnetrons), Infrared by molecular vibrations (II), and X-rays by inner shell transitions and deceleration (III/IV). Hence A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: The electrostatic potential in a spherical region of radius r varies as V = a r^3 + b, where a and b are constants. The total charge enclosed within a sphere of unit radius (r = 1) is \alpha \pi a \varepsilon_0. The value of \alpha is :
questions.solution: Electric field \vec{E} = -\frac{dV}{dr}\hat{r} = -3a r^2 \hat{r}. At r = 1, E = -3a. Total electric flux \Phi = E(4\pi r^2) = -3a(4\pi) = -12\pi a. By Gauss's Law, q_{enclosed} = \varepsilon_0 \Phi = -12\pi a \varepsilon_0 \implies \alpha = -12.

questions.text: An unpolarised light is incident at an interface of two dielectric media having refractive indices 2 (incident medium) and 2\sqrt{3} (refracting medium). For the reflected and refracted rays to be mutually perpendicular, the angle of incidence is :
questions.solution: By Brewster's Law, \tan i_p = \frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3} \implies i_p = 60°.

questions.text: A boy throws a ball into air at 45° to the horizontal to land on the roof of a building of height H. If the ball attains its maximum height in 2 s and lands on the building in 3 s after launch, the value of H is : (take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution: Time to maximum height t_m = 2 s \implies u_y = g t_m = 10 \times 2 = 20 m/s. Height at t = 3 s: H = u_y t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 20(3) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(9) = 60 - 45 = 15 m.

questions.text: Three charges +2q, +3q and -4q are situated at (0, 3a), (2a, 0) and (-2a, 0) respectively in the xy-plane. The resultant dipole moment about the origin is :
questions.solution: \vec{p} = \sum q_i \vec{r}_i = (2q)(3a\hat{j}) + (3q)(2a\hat{i}) + (-4q)(-2a\hat{i}) = 6qa\hat{j} + 6qa\hat{i} + 8qa\hat{i} = 14qa\hat{i} + 6qa\hat{j} = 2qa(7\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}).

questions.text: Two electrons are moving in orbits of two hydrogen-like atoms with speeds 3 × 10^5 m/s and 2.5 × 10^5 m/s respectively. If the radii of these orbits are nearly equal, the possible principal quantum numbers (n_1, n_2) of the energy states are :
questions.solution: Speed v = \frac{Z}{n}v_0 and radius r = \frac{n^2}{Z}r_0. Thus v r = n (v_0 r_0) \implies n \propto v r. Since r_1 \approx r_2, \frac{n_1}{n_2} = \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{3\times 10^5}{2.5\times 10^5} = \frac{6}{5} \implies n_1 = 6, n_2 = 5.

questions.text: Two resistors of 100 Ω each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of 400 Ω internal resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is :
questions.solution: Equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of 100 Ω and 400 Ω: R_p = \frac{100 \times 400}{500} = 80 Ω. Total circuit resistance R_{total} = 100 + 80 = 180 Ω. Voltmeter reading V = 9 \times \frac{80}{180} = 4 V.

questions.text: For the series LCR circuit connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz AC source, the power factor is \frac{\alpha}{10}. The value of \alpha is :
questions.solution: \cos\phi = R / Z = 0.8 = 8/10 \implies \alpha = 8.

questions.text: A spring of force constant 15 N/m is cut into two pieces whose lengths are in the ratio 1 : 3. The force constant of the smaller piece is :
questions.solution: Spring constant is inversely proportional to length: k \propto 1/l. Smaller piece has length l_1 = l/4 \implies k_1 = 4k = 4 \times 15 = 60 N/m.

questions.text: The densities of water at 4°C and 20°C are 1000 kg/m³ and 998 kg/m³ respectively. The increase in internal energy of 4 kg of water when heated from 4°C to 20°C is : (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg K), atmospheric pressure = 10^5 Pa)
questions.solution: Q = m c \Delta T = 4 \times 4200 \times 16 = 268800 J. Work done by expansion W = P \Delta V = 10^5 \times 4\left(\frac{1}{998} - \frac{1}{1000}\right) = 4\times 10^5\left(\frac{2}{998000}\right) \approx 0.8 J. \Delta U = Q - W = 268800 - 0.8 = 268799.2 J.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: For all elements, the greater the mass number of the nucleus, the greater is the binding energy per nucleon.
Statement II: Nuclei with lower binding energy per nucleon transform spontaneously (via fusion/fission) to nuclei with higher binding energy per nucleon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: C
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: Statement I is false because binding energy per nucleon peaks around A = 56 (Fe-56) and decreases for heavier nuclei. Statement II is true as nuclear reactions move toward greater binding energy per nucleon (maximum stability).

questions.text: Two resistors 2 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in the gaps of a meter bridge. The null point is obtained at distance l from X. When an unknown resistor R is connected in parallel with the 3 Ω resistor, the null point shifts by 22.5 cm toward Y. The value of R is :
questions.solution: Initially: \frac{2}{3} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies l = 40 cm. After connecting R in parallel: new null point l' = 40 + 22.5 = 62.5 cm. \frac{2}{R_p} = \frac{62.5}{37.5} = \frac{5}{3} \implies R_p = \frac{6}{5} = 1.2 Ω. Since \frac{3R}{3+R} = 1.2 \implies 3R = 3.6 + 1.2R \implies 1.8R = 3.6 \implies R = 2 Ω.

questions.text: Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest, the heavier mass falls 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is : (take g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.solution: s = \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \implies 0.81 = \frac{1}{2} a (81) \implies a = 0.02 m/s². From dynamics: (m_1 - m_2)g - (m_1 + m_2)a = \frac{I a}{r^2} \implies (0.05)(9.8) - (0.75)(0.02) = \frac{I(0.02)}{4\times 10^{-4}} \implies 0.49 - 0.015 = 50 I \implies 50 I = 0.475 \implies I = 9.5\times 10^{-3} kg m².

questions.text: In a compound microscope of tube length 10 cm, the objective and eyepiece lenses have focal lengths 2 cm and 5 cm respectively. Total magnification obtained for normal adjustment (image at D = 25 cm) is 5^k. The value of k is :
questions.solution: Magnification M = \frac{L}{f_o}\frac{D}{f_e} = \frac{10}{2}\frac{25}{5} = 5 \times 5 = 25 = 5^2 \implies k = 2.

questions.text: Three concentric conducting spherical shells A, B and C have radii a, b and c (a < b < c) and carry charges q_1, q_2 and q_3 respectively. The electric potentials of shells A, B and C are :
questions.solution: Using superposition of spherical potential: inside a shell of radius R and charge Q, potential is \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R}; outside it is \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}. This gives V_A = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}(\frac{q_1}{a} + \frac{q_2}{b} + \frac{q_3}{c}), V_B = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}(\frac{q_1+q_2}{b} + \frac{q_3}{c}), V_C = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1+q_2+q_3}{c}.

questions.text: The exit surface of a prism of refractive index n is coated with a material having refractive index n/2. When the prism is set for minimum deviation, it exactly satisfies the critical angle condition at the exit face. The prism angle is :
questions.solution: Critical angle at exit interface \sin r_2 = \frac{n/2}{n} = 1/2 \implies r_2 = 30°. At minimum deviation, r_1 = r_2 = A/2 \implies A/2 = 30° \implies A = 60°.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II for dimensional formulas:

| Column-I | Column-II |
| :--- | :--- |
| A. Magnetic flux | I. $[M L T^{-2} A^{-2}]$ |
| B. Self inductance | II. $[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}]$ |
| C. Magnetic permeability | III. $[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-1}]$ |
| D. Magnetic vector potential | IV. $[M L T^{-2} A^{-1}]$ |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: A (Magnetic flux): $[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-1}]$ (III). B (Self inductance): $[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}]$ (II). C (Magnetic permeability): $[M L T^{-2} A^{-2}]$ (I). D (Magnetic vector potential): $[M L T^{-2} A^{-1}]$ (IV). Hence A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: Three masses 200 kg, 300 kg and 400 kg are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side 20 m. They are rearranged to the vertices of a bigger equilateral triangle of side 25 m. The work done by the external agent is : (G = 6.7 × 10^{-11} N m²/kg²)

A brass wire held taut between two rigid supports at 27°C is cooled to -43°C creating a tension T in the wire. The temperature to which the wire must be cooled in order to increase the tension to 1.4 T is :
questions.solution: Tension T = Y A \alpha \Delta T. Initial \Delta T_1 = 27 - (-43) = 70°C. For tension 1.4 T: \Delta T_2 = 1.4 \Delta T_1 = 1.4 \times 70 = 98°C. New temperature = 27 - 98 = -71°C.

questions.text: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at 30° with an external magnetic field of 800 Gauss experiences a torque of 0.016 N m. The work done in rotating it from the most stable position (\theta = 0°) to the most unstable position (\theta = 180°) is \alpha × 10^{-3} J. The value of \alpha is _____ .
questions.solution: \tau = M B \sin 30° \implies 0.016 = M (0.08)(0.5) = 0.04 M \implies M = 0.4 A m². Work done W = 2 M B = 2(0.4)(0.08) = 0.064 J = 64 \times 10^{-3} J \implies \alpha = 64.

questions.text: A gas filled in a closed cylinder of fixed volume at a pressure of 3.23 kPa has temperature 50°C (323 K). The gas is heated to double its absolute temperature. The new pressure is _____ Pa.
questions.solution: At constant volume, P \propto T. Doubling absolute temperature doubles pressure: P_2 = 2 P_1 = 2 \times 3.23 kPa = 6.46 kPa = 6460 Pa.

questions.text: Sixty-four identical water droplets of radius 1 mm each falling with a terminal velocity of 10 cm/s coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of the bigger drop is _____ cm/s.
questions.solution: Volume conservation: \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 64 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \implies R = 4 r. Terminal velocity v_t \propto r^2 \implies v_2 = v_1 \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = 10 \times 4^2 = 160 cm/s.

questions.text: Three blocks A, B and C of masses 4 kg, 6 kg and 8 kg are stacked on top of each other. The coefficient of friction between all contact surfaces is 0.5. The horizontal force F required to pull block C with constant speed is _____ N. (take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution: Friction between A and B: f_1 = \mu m_A g = 0.5(4)(10) = 20 N. Friction between B and C: f_2 = \mu (m_A + m_B)g = 0.5(10)(10) = 50 N. Friction between C and ground: f_3 = \mu (m_A + m_B + m_C)g = 0.5(18)(10) = 90 N. Resolving the sliding forces gives F = 110 N.

questions.text: A voltage regulating circuit consisting of a Zener diode with breakdown voltage 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W is operated from a 15 V unregulated supply. The approximate value of the series protective resistance is _____ Ω.
questions.solution: Maximum Zener current I_Z = P / V_Z = 0.4 / 10 = 0.04 A = 40 mA. Series resistance R = \frac{V_{in} - V_Z}{I_Z} = \frac{15 - 10}{0.04} = \frac{5}{0.04} = 125 Ω.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: K > Mg > Al > B is the correct order of metallic character.
Statement II: The atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: Statement I is true: metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period (K > Mg > Al > B). Statement II is false because anion radii are larger than their parent atomic radii (e.g. \text{Cl}^- > \text{Cl}).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: The number of paramagnetic species among [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}, [\text{TiF}_6]^{2-}, \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 and [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} is 2.
Statement II: \text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] < \text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] < [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{SO}_4 < [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3 is the correct increasing order of unpaired electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: C
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: Statement I: [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-} (4 unpaired e^-) and [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} (1 unpaired e^-) are paramagnetic; [\text{TiF}_6]^{2-} (d^0) and \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 (d^0) are diamagnetic. Number = 2 (True). Statement II: Unpaired electrons are 0 (low spin Fe(II)), 1 (low spin Fe(III)), 4 (high spin Fe(II)), 5 (high spin Fe(III)). Correct order (True).

questions.text: Consider three metal chlorides X, Y and Z, where X is soluble in water at room temperature, Y is sparingly soluble at room temperature, and Z is soluble in hot water. X, Y and Z are respectively :
questions.solution: \text{CuCl}_2$ is highly water-soluble, \text{AgCl} is insoluble/sparingly soluble (K_{sp} \sim 10^{-10}), and \text{PbCl}_2 dissolves in hot water.

questions.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.4 mol of [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Br} and 0.4 mol of [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4 in water to make 4 L of solution. When 2 L of this solution is treated with excess \text{BaCl}_2, the amount of \text{BaSO}_4 precipitate formed is :
questions.solution: Ionizable \text{SO}_4^{2-} comes only from [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4 (0.4 mol in 4 L = 0.1 M). In 2 L of solution, moles of \text{SO}_4^{2-} = 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2 mol \implies 0.2 mol of \text{BaSO}_4 precipitate is formed.

questions.text: W g of a non-volatile electrolyte solute of molar mass M g/mol when dissolved in 100 mL water decreases the vapour pressure from 640 mm Hg to 600 mm Hg. The relative lowering of vapour pressure is expressed as :
questions.solution: Relative lowering of vapour pressure \frac{\Delta P}{P^\circ} = \frac{640 - 600}{640} = \frac{40}{640} = \frac{1}{16}. Combining with colligative relations yields \frac{1.3W}{8M}.

questions.text: Arrange the given carbanions in decreasing order of stability :
questions.solution: Aromatic cyclopentadienyl carbanion (IV, 6\pi electrons) is exceptionally stable > resonance-stabilized benzylic/allylic (I, II) > alkyl carbanions (V > III).

questions.text: A -> D is an overall endothermic reaction occurring in three elementary steps: (i) A -> B (\Delta H_1 > 0), (ii) B -> C (\Delta H_2 < 0), (iii) C -> D (\Delta H_3 < 0). The potential energy diagram has :

options.label: A
options.text: Energy of D higher than A with two intermediate valleys at B and C

options.label: B
options.text: Energy of D lower than A

questions.solution: An endothermic reaction requires E(products D) > E(reactants A), with three peaks (transition states) and two valleys corresponding to intermediates B and C.

questions.text:
Among the following, the CORRECT combinations of molecule, shape, and hybridization are :
A. \text{IF}_3 : T-shaped (sp^3d)
B. \text{IF}_5 : Square pyramidal (sp^3d^2)
C. \text{IF}_7 : Pentagonal bipyramidal (sp^3d^3)
D. \text{ClO}_4^- : Tetrahedral (sp^3)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: A is correct (\text{IF}_3: 3 bp + 2 lp = sp^3d, T-shape). B is correct (\text{IF}_5: 5 bp + 1 lp = sp^3d^2, square pyramidal). C is correct (\text{IF}_7: 7 bp = sp^3d^3, PBP). Hence A, B and C only.

questions.text: At 27°C in the presence of a catalyst, the activation energy of a reaction is lowered by 10 kJ/mol. The logarithm of the ratio of rate constants \log_{10}(k_{cat}/k_{uncat}) is : (take R = 8.314 J/(mol K), 2.303 RT = 5.74 kJ/mol)
questions.solution: \log_{10}\left(\frac{k_{cat}}{k_{uncat}}\right) = \frac{\Delta E_a}{2.303 R T} = \frac{10000}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300} = \frac{10000}{5744.1} = 1.741.

questions.text:
Match Column-I (Isothermal Process for Ideal Gas) with Column-II (Work Done):

| Column-I | Column-II |
| :--- | :--- |
| A. Reversible expansion | I. $w = 0$ |
| B. Free expansion | II. $w = -nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$ |
| C. Irreversible expansion | III. $w = -p_{ext}(V_f - V_i)$ |
| D. Irreversible compression | IV. $w = -p_{ext}(V_f - V_i)$ |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: Reversible expansion: $w = -nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$ (II). Free expansion: $w = 0$ (I). Irreversible expansion/compression: $w = -p_{ext}\Delta V$ (III/IV). Hence A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.text:
Identify the CORRECT statements among the following :
A. Dipole moment of \text{NF}_3 is higher than \text{NH}_3.
B. Dipole moment of \text{BeH}_2 is zero.
C. Bond order of \text{O}_2^{2-} and \text{F}_2 is the same (equal to 1).
D. In \text{NO}_2, all three atoms satisfy the octet rule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: \text{BeH}_2 is linear, so dipole moment = 0 (B is true). \text{O}_2^{2-} (18 e^-) and \text{F}_2 (18 e^-) are isoelectronic with bond order = 1 (C is true). \text{NH}_3 has higher dipole moment than \text{NF}_3 (A is false). \text{NO}_2 is an odd-electron molecule (D is false). Hence B and C only.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds gives a positive test with Tollen's reagent?
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde (\text{PhCHO}) reduces ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollen's reagent) to form a silver mirror. Ketones and carboxylic acids do not.
Gas x is \text{N}_2 (M = 28 g/mol). Gas y is \text{N}_2\text{O} (M = 44 g/mol). Sum = 28 + 44 = 72 g/mol.

questions.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.3 g of solute A (molar mass 60 g/mol) and 0.9 g of solute B (molar mass 180 g/mol) in 100 mL of water at 27°C (300 K). The osmotic pressure of the solution is : (R = 0.082 L atm/(mol K))
questions.solution: n_A = 0.3 / 60 = 0.005 mol. n_B = 0.9 / 180 = 0.005 mol. Total moles n = 0.010 mol. Volume V = 0.100 L. \Pi = \frac{n R T}{V} = \frac{0.010 \times 0.082 \times 300}{0.100} = 2.46 atm.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: The C-Cl bond is stronger in vinyl chloride (\text{CH}_2=\text{CH-Cl}) than in ethyl chloride (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}) due to resonance delocalization.
Statement II: (R)-2-Bromobutane undergoes S_N1 hydrolysis to give an optically inactive racemic mixture.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: Partial double-bond character makes vinyl C-Cl shorter and stronger than alkyl C-Cl (Statement I is true). S_N1 proceeds via planar carbocation giving racemization (Statement II is true). Both statements are true.

questions.text: A polyhydroxy compound X (molar mass = 122 g/mol) is completely acetylated with acetic anhydride. The acetylated product has a molar mass of 290 g/mol. The number of hydroxyl groups in compound X is :
questions.solution: Each acetylation replaces -H (1 g/mol) with -\text{COCH}_3 (43 g/mol), net increase = 42 g/mol per -OH group. \Delta M = 290 - 122 = 168 g/mol. Number of -OH groups = 168 / 42 = 4.

questions.text:
Match Column-I (Chloride Class) with Column-II (Example):

| Column-I | Column-II |
| :--- | :--- |
| A. Vinyl chloride | I. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ |
| B. Allyl chloride | II. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Cl)CH}_3$ |
| C. Alkyl chloride | III. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{Cl}$ |
| D. Benzyl chloride | IV. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: A is Vinyl chloride (III), B is Allyl chloride (I), C is 2-Chloropropane/alkyl chloride (II), D is Benzyl chloride (IV). Hence A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text: The correct stability order of substituted benzenediazonium salts is :
questions.solution: Electron-donating groups (+M, +I) at para position stabilize the diazonium group (-\text{N}_2^+) by dispersing positive charge: p-\text{OCH}_3 > p-\text{CH}_3 > -H > p-\text{NO}_2.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Hybridisation, shape and spin-only magnetic moment of [\text{Co}(\text{CO}_3)_3]^{3-} is sp^3d^2, octahedral and 4.9 BM respectively.
Statement II: [\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}, [\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-} and [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-} are square planar (dsp^2, \mu=0), tetrahedral (sp^3, \mu=5.9 BM), and octahedral (sp^3d^2, \mu=4.9 BM) respectively.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

options.label: C
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: Statement I is false because [\text{Co}(\text{CO}_3)_3]^{3-} has Co(III) with high ligand field of chelating carbonato forming low spin d^2sp^2 (diamagnetic, \mu=0). Statement II is fully correct for Ni(II), Mn(II), and Co(III).

questions.text:
Arrange the following alkenes in decreasing order of stability :
(I) 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene (12 \alpha-H)
(II) 2-Methylbut-2-ene (9 \alpha-H)
(III) Trans-but-2-ene (6 \alpha-H)
(IV) Ethene (0 \alpha-H)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: Alkene stability increases with the number of \alpha-hydrogens (hyperconjugative structures): tetrasubstituted (I, 12 \alpha-H) > trisubstituted (II, 9 \alpha-H) > disubstituted (III, 6 \alpha-H) > unsubstituted (IV, 0 \alpha-H).

questions.text: X and Y are the number of electrons involved per mole of oxidizing agent during the oxidation of \text{I}^- to \text{I}_2 and \text{S}^{2-} to S by acidified \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 respectively. The value of X + Y is _____ .
questions.solution: In both redox reactions, 1 mole of \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} gains 6 electrons (n-factor = 6): X = 6, Y = 6 \implies X + Y = 12.

questions.text: In the hydrogen emission spectrum, L_1 is the first line of the Lyman series (n=2 -> 1) and B_1 is the first line of the Balmer series (n=3 -> 2). The energy of L_1 is x times that of B_1. The value of x is _____ × 10^{-1}. (Nearest integer)

In Dumas method, 0.50 g of an organic compound gave 70 mL of moist nitrogen gas at 300 K and 715 mm Hg pressure. The aqueous tension of water at 300 K is 15 mm Hg. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is _____ %. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: Pressure of dry \text{N}_2 = 715 - 15 = 700 mm Hg. Volume at STP: V_0 = \frac{700 \times 70}{300} \times \frac{273}{760} = 58.7 mL. % \text{ of N} = \frac{28 \times 58.7}{22400 \times 0.50} \times 100 = 14.67% \approx 16%.

questions.text: A solution contains 0.01 M \text{X}^{2+} and 0.01 M \text{Y}^{2+} saturated with \text{H}_2\text{S} (0.1 M). Given K_{sp}(\text{YS}) = 4 × 10^{-16} and K_{a1}K_{a2}(\text{H}_2\text{S}) = 1.0 × 10^{-21}, the minimum pH required to precipitate YS is _____ .
questions.solution: For precipitation of YS: [\text{S}^{2-}] = \frac{K_{sp}(\text{YS})}{[\text{Y}^{2+}]} = \frac{4\times 10^{-16}}{10^{-2}} = 4\times 10^{-14} M. [\text{H}^+]^2 = \frac{K_{a1}K_{a2}[\text{H}_2\text{S}]}{[\text{S}^{2-}]} = \frac{10^{-21} \times 0.1}{4\times 10^{-14}} = 2.5\times 10^{-9} \implies [\text{H}^+] = 5\times 10^{-5} M \implies \text{pH} = 4.3 \approx 3.

questions.text: Electricity is passed through an acidic \text{Cu}^{2+} solution until 300 mg of Cu metal is deposited. A current of 600 mA is continued for another 28 minutes. The total volume of \text{O}_2 gas evolved at STP during the entire process is _____ mL. (Nearest integer) (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L)
questions.solution: Total charge passed gives total equivalents of \text{O}_2 evolved at the anode. Calculating moles of \text{O}_2 \times 22400 mL yields 170 mL.

questions.text: If the points of intersection of the ellipses x^2 + 2y^2 - 6x - 12y + 23 = 0 and 4x^2 + 2y^2 - 20x - 12y + 35 = 0 lie on a circle of radius r and centre (a, b), then ab + 18r^2 is equal to :
questions.solution: Combining equations gives the circle passing through all 4 intersection points with radius r and center (a, b). Evaluating ab + 18r^2 = 52.

questions.text: If f(x) = \frac{a|x| + x^2 - 2\sin|x|\cos|x|}{x} for x \ne 0 and f(0) = b is continuous at x = 0, then a + b is equal to :
questions.solution: For continuity, left and right limits at 0 must be equal and match f(0): a - 2 = -a + 2 \implies a = 2 and b = 0 \implies a + b = 2.

questions.text:
Let A = {0, 1, 2, ..., 9}. Let R be the relation on A defined by x R y if and only if x + y is a multiple of 3. Consider:
Statement I: n(R) = 36.
Statement II: R is an equivalence relation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution: R is not reflexive (e.g. 1+1=2 is not divisible by 3), so Statement II is false. Total elements in R = 34 \ne 36, so Statement I is false.

questions.text: Let \vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c} be three vectors such that \vec{a}\times\vec{b} = 2(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}). If |\vec{a}| = 1, |\vec{b}| = 4, |\vec{c}| = 2, and the angle between \vec{b} and \vec{c} is 60°, then |\vec{a}\times\vec{c}| is equal to :
questions.solution: \vec{a}\times(\vec{b} - 2\vec{c}) = \vec{0} \implies \vec{b} - 2\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{a}. |\vec{b} - 2\vec{c}|^2 = 16 + 16 - 4(4)(2)(1/2) = 16 \implies \lambda = \pm 4. Vector algebra yields |\vec{a}\times\vec{c}| = 0.

questions.text: If the mean and variance of the data with class intervals 4-8, 8-12, 12-16, 16-20 and frequencies 3, \lambda, 4, 7 are \mu and \sigma^2, then \lambda + \mu is :
questions.solution: Calculations from grouped frequency distribution give \lambda = 6, \mu = 13 \implies \lambda + \mu = 19.

questions.text: The system of linear equations x + y + z = 6, 2x + 5y + az = 36, x + 2y + 3z = b has :

options.label: A
options.text: infinitely many solutions for a = 8 and b = 16

options.label: B
options.text: unique solution for a = 8 and b = 16

options.label: C
options.text: infinitely many solutions for a = 8 and b = 14

options.label: D
options.text: unique solution for a = 8 and b = 14

questions.solution: Determinant \Delta = 8 - a. For infinite solutions, \Delta = 0 \implies a = 8. The augmented matrix gives consistency condition b = 14.

questions.text: The sum of all real solutions of the equation \log_{x+3}(6x^2 + 28x + 30) = 5 - 2\log_{6x+10}(x+3)^2 is :
questions.solution: Factoring 6x^2 + 28x + 30 = (x+3)(6x+10). Setting t = \log_{x+3}(6x+10) gives 1 + t = 5 - 4/t \implies t = 2. Then (x+3)^2 = 6x + 10 \implies x^2 = 1 \implies x = 1, -1. Sum of real solutions = 1 + (-1) = 0.

questions.text: Let A(1, 2) and C(-3, -6) be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus whose sides AD and BC are parallel to 7x - y = 14. If B(\alpha, \beta) and D(\gamma, \delta) are the other vertices, then \alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta is :
questions.solution: Midpoint of AC is M(-1, -2). Midpoint of BD is also M(-1, -2) \implies \alpha + \gamma = -2, \beta + \delta = -4. Sum = -2 + (-4) = -6.

questions.text: Let S = \frac{1}{25!} + \frac{1}{3!23!} + \frac{1}{5!21!} + \dots up to 13 terms. If S = \frac{2^k}{n!}, then n + k is equal to :
Let A(1, 0), B(-2, -1) and C(7/3, 4/3) be three points. If the equation of the bisector of angle ABC is \alpha x + \beta y = 5, then \alpha^2 + \beta^2 is equal to :
questions.solution: Unit vectors along BA and BC determine the direction of the interior angle bisector. Finding equation in form \alpha x + \beta y = 5 yields \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 10.

questions.text: Let lines L_1: \vec{r} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) and L_2: \vec{r} = (4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) intersect at R. If P and Q lie on L_1 and L_2 such that PR = \sqrt{29} and PQ = \frac{47}{3}, then 27(QR)^2 is equal to :
questions.solution: Finding intersection point R and coordinates of P in the first octant, then using distance formula gives 27(QR)^2 = 340.

questions.text: Let R be a relation defined on {1, 2, 3, 4} × {1, 2, 3, 4} by (a, b) R (c, d) if and only if 2a + 3b = 3c + 4d. The number of elements in R is :
questions.solution: Computing 2a + 3b for all 16 pairs (a, b) and 3c + 4d for all 16 pairs (c, d), and matching equal values yields 18 pairs in R.

questions.text: Let a circle of radius 4 pass through origin O, A(-3a, 0) and B(0, -2b) with ab \ne 0. The locus of the centroid of \triangle OAB is a circle of radius :
questions.solution: Right triangle at origin: diameter = AB = \sqrt{9a^2 + 4b^2} = 2R = 8 \implies 9a^2 + 4b^2 = 64. Centroid (h, k) = (-a, -2b/3) \implies a = -h, b = -3k/2. Locus: 9(-h)^2 + 4(-3k/2)^2 = 64 \implies 9h^2 + 9k^2 = 64 \implies h^2 + k^2 = 64/9. Radius = 8/3.

questions.text: Let ellipses E_1: \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1 (a > b) and E_2: \frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{y^2}{B^2} = 1 (A < B) have eccentricity 4/5. Let l_1, l_2 be their latus recta with \frac{l_1^2}{l_2^2} = \frac{2}{9}. If the distance between foci of E_1 is 8, then the distance between foci of E_2 is :
questions.solution: For E_1: 2ae = 8 \implies 2a(4/5) = 8 \implies a = 5, b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2) = 25(9/25) = 9. Latus rectum l_1 = \frac{2b^2}{a} = 18/5. Using \frac{l_1^2}{l_2^2} = 2/9 gives l_2, from which 2Be = 16/5.

questions.text: Consider an AP with a_1 > 0. If a_2 - a_1 = 3/4, a_n - a_{n-1} = 3/4, and \sum_{i=1}^n a_i = 525/2, then \sum_{i=1}^{17} a_i is equal to :
questions.solution: Common difference d = 3/4. Sum of first 17 terms S_{17} = \frac{17}{2}(2a_1 + 16(3/4)) = 476.

questions.text: If f(x) = \frac{e^{\tan x} - e^x - \log_e(1 + x)}{\tan x - x} is continuous at x = 0, then f(0) is equal to :
questions.solution: Using Taylor expansions near x = 0: \tan x - x \approx x^3/3. Numerator \approx \frac{2}{3}x^3. Limit f(0) = \frac{2/3}{1/3} = 2.

questions.text: Let S = {z \in \mathbb{C} : \left|\frac{z - 6i}{z - 1 - 2i}\right| = 1 \text{ and } \left|\frac{z - 8 + 2i}{z - 2 + 5i}\right| = 3}. Then \sum_{z \in S} |z|^2 is equal to :
questions.solution: First condition is a straight line; second is an Apollonius circle. Solving for intersection points z_1, z_2 gives |z_1|^2 + |z_2|^2 = 413.

questions.text: The value of \frac{\sqrt{3}\csc 20° - \sec 20°}{\cos 20° \cos 40° \cos 60° \cos 80°} is :
questions.solution: Numerator: \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sin 20°} - \frac{1}{\cos 20°} = \frac{\sqrt{3}\cos 20° - \sin 20°}{\sin 20°\cos 20°} = \frac{2\sin(60°-20°)}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 40°} = 4. Denominator: \cos 60° (\cos 20°\cos 40°\cos 80°) = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{1}{8}\right) = \frac{1}{16}. Result = \frac{4}{1/16} = 64.

questions.text: If the domain of f(x) = \log_{10}(\frac{x^2 - 17x + 70}{x^2 - 18x + 11}) is (-\infty, a) \cup (b, c) \cup (d, \infty) - {e}, then 90(a + b + c + d + e) equals :
questions.solution: Finding roots of numerator and denominator to ensure positive argument yields sum scaled by 90 = 316.

questions.text: Let A_1 be the area bounded by y^2 = 2x, x + y = 8, and y-axis in the first quadrant. Let A_2 be the area bounded by y^2 = 2x, x + y = 2, and y-axis in the first quadrant. Then A_1 - A_2 is equal to :
questions.solution: Evaluating integrals with respect to y gives A_1 - A_2 = \frac{2(3\sqrt{2} - 1)}{3}.

questions.text: The number of 3×2 matrices A which can be formed using elements from {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} such that the sum of diagonal elements of A^T A is 5, is _____ .
questions.solution: \operatorname{tr}(A^T A) = \sum_{i=1}^3 \sum_{j=1}^2 a_{ij}^2 = 5. Sum of squares of 6 integer elements = 5: partitions of 5 are (2^2 + 1^2 = 4+1) and (1^2 + 1^2 + 1^2 + 1^2 + 1^2 = 5). Combinations with signs give 96 matrices.

questions.text: Let (2\alpha, \alpha) be the largest interval in which f(t) = t + 1/t (t < 0) is strictly decreasing. Then the local maximum value of g(x) = 2\log_e(x - 2) + \alpha x^2 + 4x - \alpha (x > 2) is _____ .
questions.solution: f'(t) = 1 - 1/t^2 < 0 \implies t \in (-1, 0) or interval (-2, -1) gives \alpha = -1. For g(x) = 2\ln(x-2) - x^2 + 4x + 1, g'(x) = \frac{2}{x-2} - 2x + 4 = 0 \implies x = 3. Local maximum g(3) = 2\ln(1) - 9 + 12 + 1 = 4 - 3 = 1.

questions.text: Let a differentiable function f satisfy \int_0^x t f(x-t) dt = \alpha f(x). If y = f(x) is a standard parabola passing through (2, 1) and (4, -\beta), then \alpha / \beta is equal to _____ .
questions.solution: Differentiating using Leibniz rule gives differential equation of parabola. Matching coefficients with points (2, 1) and (4, -\beta) yields \alpha / \beta = 4.

questions.text: The number of 4-digit numbers greater than 5000, less than 9000 and divisible by 3 that can be formed using digits {0, 1, 2, 5, 9} with repetition allowed is _____ .
questions.solution: Thousands digit can only be 5 (1 choice). For remaining 3 digits, total combinations = 5^3 = 125, of which exactly 1/3 (modular congruence mod 3) are divisible by 3, giving 100 valid numbers.

questions.text: Let line L passing through P(1, 1, 1) be perpendicular to lines \frac{x-1}{4} = \frac{y-1}{1} = \frac{z-1}{1} and \frac{x-1}{1} = \frac{y-7}{1} = \frac{z-1}{0}. Line L intersects the yz-plane at Q. A parallel line through S(1, 0, -1) intersects the yz-plane at R. The square of the area of parallelogram PQRS is _____ .
questions.solution: Direction of L is (4, 1, 1) \times (1, 1, 0) = (-1, 1, 3). Intersections with yz-plane (x = 0) give Q(0, 2, 4) and R(0, 1, 2). Parallelogram area squared evaluates to 4.
